articles.title: Former Australia sprint champion Jake Doran charged with alleged child abuse
articles.summary: Police charge 26-year-old with indecent treatment of child under 16. Australian Athletics ban sprinter from any involvement in the sport. Australia’s 2022 men’s 100m sprint champion has been arrested in Townsville for alleged indecent treatment of children.
body: Queensland police arrested Jake Doran on 13 October and he has been charged with one count of “indecent treatment of child under 16 (indecent film etc)”. Police investigations covered the period between January 2025 and September 2026. The 26-year-old was bailed to appear at Townsville magistrates court on 5 November.
Doran, who works in business development at Tafe Queensland, has been training athletes in Townsville.
Australian Athletics confirmed he has no paid or unpaid role with the national governing body, but has banned him from any involvement in the sport while the matter is ongoing.

“Based on information provided to Australian Athletics, the organisation has imposed a provisional action on the athlete, prohibiting him from attending club, member association or Australian Athletics events, as well as banning him from participating in athletics training,” a spokesperson said.
points: Police charge 26-year-old with indecent treatment of child under 16.

articles.title: ‘It doesn’t look good’: Arteta concerned as Saka limps off against Bayern Munich
articles.summary: ‘A player off with really sharp pain is never good news’ Winger forced off 10 minutes into Arsenal’s 2-2 draw. Mikel Arteta made no attempt to conceal his concern over the quad injury that forced Bukayo Saka out of Arsenal’s 2-2 Champions League draw at Bayern Munich, saying it did not “look good…
body: The manager was delighted with the fight that his players showed, Declan Rice earning a deserved point with an 82nd-minute equaliser. Arsenal had led through Eberechi Eze, who came on in the 10th minute for the stricken Saka, before Harry Kane took centre stage. The Bayern striker set up Alphonso Davies for 1-1 before giving his team the lead from the penalty spot.

It was Saka’s setback that provided the sour note for Arsenal. He collapsed to the turf after a routine battle with Davies and walked off slowly after treatment. Saka was still moving in a very limited way as he left the stadium.

“It doesn’t look good at all but we have to wait and see,” Arteta said. “They [the medics] are a bit concerned. A player who has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news. Bukayo did not start the game against Lille last Tuesday, then he started at Nottingham Forest on Sunday and it happened very early in this game. The level of intensity that this game requires, as well, is something incredible.

articles.title: Goal, assist... goal-kick - Kane underlines Ballon d'Or credentials
articles.summary: Why Declan Rice backs his England team-mate Harry Kane to win the Ballon d'Or after Arsenal's draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League.
body: There were fewer than 25 minutes on the clock during Bayern Munich's thrilling 2-2 draw with Arsenal in the Champions League when the forward took matters into his own hands in a bid to break the deadlock.
As the Premier League champions prepared to defend a Bayern goal-kick, Kane seized the initiative by launching his side up the pitch with a raking 80-yard pass.
It was a moment of remarkable ingenuity from the England international, one that almost ended with Bayern taking the lead.
"Under Vincent Kompany, he has been given a level of trust that he has probably never had before under any other manager," former Manchester City defender Nedum Onuoha told BBC Sport.

articles.title: Champions League: Silva sparks Real Madrid’s demolition of Leipzig as Lask stun Sporting
articles.summary: Bernardo Silva opens scoring as Madrid win 4-1. Galatasaray sweep past Lille; 10-man Inter edge Shakhtar. Real Madrid claimed a third Champions League victory in as many games by thrashing RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday, with Kylian Mbappé and Yan Diomande among the goals for José Mourinho’s side.
body: Bernardo Silva opened the scoring for Madrid from close range towards the end of a tight first half, with Arda Guler doubling the record 15-time European champions’ advantage soon after the interval.
Mbappé bent home a third before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back for the German side and Diomande rammed a volley into the top corner to cap Madrid’s triumph late on.

“We know every point is important to get into the top eight, we know we have to win as many games as possible – we’ve won three and there are five to go,” Mbappé said. The France forward, who hopes to win the Ballon d’Or next week, has netted in each of Madrid’s Champions League matches this season and has 12 goals in 12 games.

“I’m doing well [but] I think I can do more,” he said. “I’m one of the few players who always has to demand more from himself... right now it’s a good moment, but we have to keep going and I have to do more.”

articles.title: ‘Angry’ Carrick on the brink as Fernandes hits out at Manchester United tactics
articles.summary: Manager apologises to fans after 4-1 defeat in Como. Captain criticises ‘decision from the staff’ not to press. Michael Carrick’s future as Manchester United manager is in the balance after a humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como on Wednesday night.
body: Before Bournemouth’s visit to Old Trafford on Sunday his future may be discussed by Jason Wilcox, the director of football, Omar Berrada, the chief executive, and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the co-owner who controls sporting policy.

On a torrid night an “angry” ­Carrick insisted afterwards that he had not given his position any thought and was forced to defend himself against Bruno Fernandes after his captain questioned the manager’s tactics of not pressing against Cesc Fàbregas’s team. Carrick also criticised his side for not running. The defeat by Como in the third Champions League group game leaves United with only two wins all season from 11 games. ­Carrick’s side are in 13th place in the Premier League and were eliminated from the Carabao Cup last month.

The 45-year-old was asked if he fears for his job. “Listen, I’ve not given my own position any thought,” he said. “[My thoughts are] for the supporters – I was one of them watching that and I wasn’t happy at all.”

body: The 25-year-old winger went down in the 10th minute at Allianz Arena - attempting to play a pass with nobody around him - and had to be replaced by Eberechi Eze, who went on to score the opening goal.
"They are a bit concerned. A player who has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see," Arteta told TNT Sports.
Saka has had fitness issues in recent months and his game time was managed at the end of last season, as well as with England at the World Cup, because of an Achilles injury he picked up in March.
He missed the March international break and seven games for the Gunners, but returned to help them lift the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years.

articles.title: Player Ratings: Real Madrid 4–1 RB Leipzig
articles.summary: Thibaut Courtois: 8.5. Made five saves, including two outstanding stops. Another performance in which his interventions were crucial, even if the final score suggests a comfortable evening. Fede Valverde: 9. Dominant at right-back.
body: Fede Valverde: 9. Dominant at right-back. His movement helped create relentless overloads down the right, and his distribution kept Madrid’s attacks flowing. Finished with three key passes and a game-high 116 touches, while contributing four tackles, five clearances, and a goal-saving defensive intervention. An enormous contribution on both sides of the ball.
Antonio Rüdiger: 7. Good in possession and produced an excellent recovery to stop Cardoso from breaking through in the first half.

Dean Huijsen: 7.5. His vertical distribution and long-range passing were brilliant, helping Madrid advance the ball and find teammates beyond Leipzig’s pressure. Could have defended the conceded goal better, but also registered seven interceptions and earned a couple of ovations from the Bernabéu for his defensive interventions.
Álvaro Carreras: 5. Looked short of confidence. His passing down the flank was poor, and some ill-advised defensive gambles left him exposed.

articles.title: Teenager with cerebral palsy hits first baseball into the outfield
articles.summary: Carson Hawkins, a 16-year-old with quadriplegic cerebral palsy, hit a baseball into the grass for the first time during a game in Stanley. A security camera captured the hit two weeks ago. Carson’s mother, Erin Hawkins, explained that her son has lived with physical limitations since birth.
body: “Carson had a rough delivery. He went 6 minutes without oxygen. He has quadriplegic cerebral palsy,” Erin Hawkins said. She added that “he’s always loved the game of baseball.”
Hitting the ball required years of practice for Carson. When asked how it felt to swing and miss repeatedly during his early efforts, Carson said, “Terrible.”
Despite the early difficulty, hitting the ball strengthened his dedication to the sport. “It made me love it more,” Carson said. He lives by a clear personal motto: “Don’t give up.”

Freddie Dow, Carson’s baseball coach in Stanley, placed him on two youth league teams. Dow arranged with opposing teams to let Carson lead off the inning three times per game, allowing him to round the bases after each hit.

articles.title: Miserable Man Utd ripped apart by Como
articles.summary: Michael Carrick's Manchester United were ripped apart in a dreadful 4-1 defeat at Como in the Champions League, as their miserable run of results stretched to seven without a win.
body: The pressure continues to pile on Carrick and this United side as their start to the season lurches from bad to worse - and on Wednesday night they were humbled by a Como team that delivered more intensity and quality in Italy.

The first attribute should be a non-negotiable but, despite United's application being in the spotlight, they were once again outworked by their opposition. Static in midfield, allowing Como players to run off them, losing markers... this was a shocking show of United's big failings out of possession.

The tone was set just two minutes in when Man Utd went behind early on - again. They are the first English side to concede in back-to-back Champions League games so soon and never got to grips with Cesc Fabregas' impressively coached team.

Nico Paz brought the class for the hosts. The talented Argentina international stuck the opener into the top corner when Harry Maguire gave him too much space and then slotted in a third after catching Carlos Baleba in possession.

articles.title: England 'not thinking about points difference' against France
articles.summary: England hooker Brad O'Neill says his side will resist the urge to go for broke when they face France in their second Rugby League World Cup match in Perth on Saturday.
body: An opening 30-12 defeat to Tonga has left their hopes of reaching the semi-finals hanging by a thread, with points difference looking increasingly like the only way to progress.
But head coach Brian McDermott has named an unchanged 19-man matchday squad, a sign that he does not plan radical changes against a France team smarting from their 78-4 humbling by Samoa.
O'Neill, the newly-crowned Super League Man of Steel, said: "We have discussed what is required but I feel like the mentality can't be any different to what we had against Tonga.

"We can't go into this game thinking about the points difference. We've got to go into this game hard-nosed like we did against Tonga, and hopefully if we do our jobs well enough we're going to get the win."

articles.title: England star Kildunne dropped for Canada rematch
articles.summary: Ellie Kildunne has been dropped to the bench in the England Red Roses squad to face Canada on Friday, a week on from suffering defeat in Toronto which ended a 41-match unbeaten run.
body: Head coach John Mitchell has made four changes to the starting XV in total, with Gloucester-Hartpury duo Emma Sing and Mia Venner coming into the back three at full-back and wing respectively, while Helena Rowland of Loughborough Lightning returns at inside-centre.
In the forwards, there is just one amendment to the team that began the second Test - Sadia Kabeya, also of Loughborough Lightning, is selected at openside flanker.
While Kildunne - 2024's World Player of the Year - and back-row Alex Matthews move to the replacements bench, wing Claudia Moloney-MacDonald and centre Tatyana Heard drop out of the squad altogether.

"Last Friday, we lost sight of what we could control when it mattered most; that's on us to fix. This week is about getting back to who we are: hungry, accountable to each other and demanding more of ourselves than anyone outside this group ever could.
